title: Xi, Putin meet in China, ahead of summit with Trump
summary: China's President Xi Jinping on Wednesday pledged to stand up against trade protectionism, while his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin criticized Western sanctions as the two set the stage for a…

image.caption: In this pool photograph distributed by the Russian state agency Sputnik, Russia's President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping shake hands Wednesday prior to a meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China. (Sergei Bobylyov/AFP/Getty Images)

blocks.text: World·New

China's President Xi Jinping on Wednesday pledged to stand up against trade protectionism, while his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin criticized Western sanctions as the two set the stage for a high-stakes trilateral meeting with ‌U.S. President Donald Trump.
Other countries watch with great interest as leaders of 3 powers prepare to meet

They delivered their speeches at an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen, hours before Trump landed in China after meeting key regional allies in Manila this week.

Xi greeted Trump at the airport, reciprocating the U.S. president's gesture at Joint Base Andrews in September when they last met. They had a brief hug and a short exchange before walking along the red carpet to their motorcades.
The two will participate in an APEC group photo and attend a banquet with other leaders.

They will meet ​with Putin on the sidelines on Thursday and potentially discuss Russia's war with Ukraine and the U.S. war ​with Iran, as well as other flashpoints such as trade, AI and nuclear weapons.

The meeting has drawn comparisons with the 1945 Yalta Conference between the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union that formalized spheres of influence, set the stage for the post-Second World War order and became shorthand for great-power deals imposed on smaller countries.
What to know about Canada and China's new trade pact
It has also ​unnerved some European and Asian capitals, who fear the world's greatest military powers will disregard their interests.
The Wall Street Journal, in an editorial, said it was "a sign of Mr. Trump’s mercurial foreign policy that the [summit] is creating more anxiety among allies than adversaries."

The Kremlin this week dismissed comparisons with the Yalta Conference as "games of political scientists," but said the meeting will have a major impact on global affairs. Beijing said the trilateral will promote world peace.

blocks.text: In his opening address, Xi urged support for what he ⁠called "free and open trade," trying to portray his ⁠country as a stable partner on the global stage, in contrast with the U.S., which has raised tariffs and ‌adopted a more muscular foreign policy under Trump.

Xi's remarks came after Washington announced further restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips from companies such as Nvidia, which could further complicate a fragile trade truce with Beijing. China has pledged to retaliate.

"We must firmly uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core, support free and open trade and investment, maintain the stability and smooth operation of global industrial and supply chains," Xi told an audience of business executives.
Dancers wave Russian and Chinese flags during the welcoming ceremony for Putin on Wednesday. (Anupam Nath/The Associated Press)
Western trade partners have ⁠criticized China for running annual trade surpluses exceeding $1 trillion US through policies that support its manufacturing sector at the expense of its consumers.

Beijing says its growth model is appropriate for an economy still catching up with the world's richest, but the U.S., the European Union in Brussels and others are concerned about China's supply chain dominance providing the country with geopolitical leverage and say its policies threaten their industries and jobs.

Xi said China will continue to invest in its industrial complex and ‌develop new technologies that would also benefit other countries. The world's second-largest economy will lower tariffs and further open up its markets, while standing up against protectionism and unilateralism, he added.

His "message is likely to resonate with many Global South countries and reinforces Beijing's effort to contrast its technology strategy with that of Washington," said George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group.

blocks.text: Trump's trip to Asia is his first since his Republican Party's defeat in midterm elections, while allegations involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy ​add to the tension.

Trump has downplayed the allegations, having developed a close relationship with Huang over the past two years, and both he and his Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have faced questions over when they knew about the allegations, given weighty decisions that were made by the White House over export controls on Nvidia chips.

blocks.text: Most analysts expect Washington and Beijing to keep ties relatively stable as Trump and Xi are set to follow their meeting in Shenzhen with their fourth of the year at the Group of 20 gathering in Miami in December.

Putin, who was speaking after ⁠Ukraine crippled the vital Kerch road bridge linking Crimea to Russia in a major blow to his four-year-old war, followed Xi on stage with a speech that described Western powers as "former hegemons."
U.S. President Donald Trump and Xi applaud as the U.S. leader arrives at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport on Wednesday. (Mandel Ngan/Getty Images)
He said Europe ⁠was in a "humiliating decline" and that anti-Russian sanctions imposed after his invasion of Ukraine had backfired.
"Experience has shown that the traditional tools of economic dominance and de facto coercion have largely run their ⁠course, having lost much ⁠of their intimidating power," Putin said.
"While sanctions, tariffs, and export restrictions ​may still exert a certain deterrent effect, they are incapable of halting growth — let alone crushing the economies of competitors."
Ukraine's strike on Putin's bridge carries symbolic weight. Will it change the war?
Putin described the world as "turbulent" but said disagreements can be addressed by "sitting at the table."
"I therefore expect big potential benefit from the upcoming trilateral meeting," he said.
On Tuesday, Taiwan and Japan flagged incursions by Russian aircraft into their airspace.
In a bilateral meeting later, Xi and Putin praised their close partnership and pledged more measures that advance ​a "multipolar world."

In Manila, Trump vowed to deepen defence co-operation ⁠with the Philippines, amid its growing friction with Beijing over disputed features in the South China Sea. Earlier, he floated the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China, but that has not been confirmed.
